paper text.text: Suppose neither $h_b$ nor $bc$ occurs. Contract $cf$ and take a torus embedding of this proper minor. Identify the two boundary copies of $P_1$ in its incident facial disks, keeping all other boundary appearances distinct. The path $P_1$ then lies inside the resulting region apart from its ends. By the rotation table~\supp{R3}, this region is either the annulus $ac\mid bd$ or a disk with attachment sequence $a,c,b,d,c$ or $a,c,b,c,d,c$. Every $\Psi_1$-bridge inside $B$ meets the interior of $P_1$, so lies in this region. No other face contains both $a,d$, so any present $h_a$ or $ad$ lies there too. The annulus would make $H_1$ planar by Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding}. The first disk would make $H_1+bc+cd$ planar by Lemma~\ref{lem:embedding-extension}, so $H_1$ would again be planar. Both contradict its nonplanarity. Thus only the last disk occurs. Joining its consecutive attachments gives the edges $ac,bc,cd$, so $(B\cup H_{\mathrm{ext}})+ac+bc+cd$ is planar. Its subgraph $H_1-bd$ is therefore planar, which means every $K_{3,3}$ subdivision of $H_1$, including $H_2'$, uses $bd$. If neither $h_a$ nor $ad$ occurs, contracting $ed$ instead gives $H_1-ac$ planar, so every such subdivision uses $ac$. Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} therefore lists every possible $B$ using the six choices of $H_{\mathrm{ext}}$, the added edges $ac,bd$, and the subdivision edges and planar completions required above. Adjoining $J_1\cup J_2$, the edges $cf,ed$ and the chosen $H_{\mathrm{ext}}$ to each candidate gives the graphs to be checked. The checks in~\supp{E6} leave only $\mathfrak T_{21}$ and $\mathfrak T_{63}$.

what: Every rotation system of Psi_1/cf in the notation of Proposition 4.25 (a = s1, b = t1, c = s2, d = t3, e = s3, f = t2; the paths are the edges ab, cf, ed, and f is contracted into c). Attachments a, b, c, d; twins and e omitted.
how to read: For each graph: 'cyclic orders' lists, for every vertex, all cyclic orders of its neighbours, each starting with its alphabetically first neighbour (the other neighbours follow in every possible order, in lexicographic order). Rotation system number i (counting from 0) takes at each vertex the cyclic order whose position is the corresponding digit of i, written in the mixed radix given by the numbers of cyclic orders in the order of 'vertices', the last vertex varying fastest (the order of Python's itertools.product). Facial walks are traced by the rule used throughout the supplement: after the dart u->v comes v->w, where w follows u in the cyclic order at v. The genus is (2 - V + E - F)/2. The attachment sequence of a facial walk lists the attachments it passes through, in walk order, one entry per passage; it is written from its lexicographically least cyclic shift, keeping the direction of the walk, and the faces of a row are sorted. Since many rotation systems give the same row, the distinct rows are listed once under 'distinct rows' and 'rows' gives, for every rotation system in order, the position of its row in that list. 'Up to cyclic shift and reversal' in the claims means the least sequence among all cyclic shifts of the sequence and of its reverse.

graphs.name: Psi_1/cf (a = s1, b = t1, c = s2, d = t3, e = s3, f = t2; f contracted into c)
graphs.row format: [genus, attachment sequences of the facial walks, for a torus rotation the region along P_1 = ab, up to cyclic shift and reversal]

claims.statement: Psi_1/cf is connected and nonplanar, so its torus embeddings are cellular.

The torus embeddings of Psi_1/cf give exactly three regions incident with P_1 whose boundary contains both c, d: ac | bd (annulus) with a, bc, cd, cd in the other faces; a,c,b,d,c with a, bcd, cd; a,c,b,c,d,c with a, bd, cd (up to cyclic shift and reversal).
